f2.quote: The optimum reported annealing condition was 550 °C for 2 h. Hardness improved at 400–550 °C but declined at 700–850 °C.

f3.quote: Electrochemical testing used 3.5 wt% H2SO4 with saturated calomel reference and Pt counter electrodes.

f4.quote: Hot-corrosion testing was conducted at 900 °C for ten 5 h cycles (50 h total) under mixture A (75% Na2SO4/25% NaCl), B (70% Na2SO4/20% NaCl/10% V2O5), or C (60% Na2SO4/20% NaCl/20% V2O5).

f5.quote: At 550 °C, annealing produced a dense, refined grain structure with an average grain size near 15 µm, approximately 80% more low-angle than high-angle grain-boundary fraction, fewer voids, and retained major BCC/minor FCC phases.

f6.quote: Grain refinement and the major BCC phase impede dislocation motion and increase hardness.

f7.quote: rapid formation of stable Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides restrict pit and crack development and impede sulphide attack.
